question: A 20-year-old stared at the 2017 eclipse. How long until permanent damage?
answer: Six seconds was enough. The eclipse burned the centre of her retina for good (solar retinopathy), leaving a scotoma: a black spot right where she looks.
move: Never look at the sun with the naked eye: seconds can scar the retina for life.

web.label: A draggable pin on a time scale asks how long a 20-year-old stared at the 2017 eclipse, followed by a choice of how sure you are. The reveal states that six seconds was enough to leave a permanent black spot in her central vision.
